title: Tiered renewal repricing & security RFQ integration playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a set of pragmatic experiments and runbooks to (1) introduce tiered repricing bands for enterprise renewals and expansions, (2) automate true-up cadence for usage-driven contracts, and (3) integrate security/RFQ questionnaire completion as an eligibility gate for multi-year discounts. The aim is to reduce revenue leakage, standardize commercial outcomes across reps, and protect margin while preserving a clear path for expanded customer adoption.

Scope:
- Applicable to enterprise accounts (TCV > $250k) and accounts with Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Focus on renewals, contraction/expansion true-ups, and multi-year discount eligibility rules.
- Include integration with Security Questionnaire (SQ) status so that unanswered/failed SQs block discount application until remediated.
- Deliverables: repricing bands decision matrix, automated true-up workflow, SFDC and Contract template changes, in-console messaging copy, and internal playbook for AE/CS.

Proposal summary:
1) Tiered repricing bands: introduce three renewal bands based on trailing 12-month average spend growth and adoption signals (Usage Growth, Route Count, Embedding Units):
   - Band A (Baseline): <= 10% growth — standard renewal pricing, 0-5% one-time uplift credits available.
   - Band B (Adopt): 11-40% growth — eligible for 5-12% uplift discounts if adoption milestones achieved and SQ is completed.
   - Band C (Scale): >40% growth — eligible for 12-25% multi-year discounts with mandatory 12- or 24-month commit and passed SQ.

2) True-up automation: quarterly auto true-up (QTU) with optional customer opt-out at contract signature:
   - QTU triggers: monthly usage average > committed baseline by >10% for two consecutive months OR end-of-quarter overage >5%.
   - Mechanic: system creates draft invoice and notifies AE/CS. If customer raises dispute, AE has 10 business days to flag. If unresolved, auto-invoice executes.
   - Backbilling cap: true-ups may be backbilled up to 90 days from event; exceptions require legal signoff.

3) Security/RFQ integration as a gating signal for discounts:
   - SQ Status values: completed-passed, pending, failed. Discounts >10% require completed-passed SQ within last 12 months.
   - Implementation: SFDC field + console contract flow check that prevents discount code application if SQ status != completed-passed.

4) Grace & remediation: for accounts that fail SQ or are pending, provide conditional uplift credits (1-3%) instead of larger discounts and a remediation window (60 days) to pass SQ for previously approved discounts to be applied retroactively.

Operational considerations and constraints:
- Accounting implications: QTU requires invoice automation and GL mapping for mid-cycle charges — AP and RevOps sign-off required.
- Legal & compliance: multi-year commits need contract clauses for early termination and audit rights; send to Legal for template language.
- Sales enablement: AE playbook with scripts for SQ enablement and migration incentives.
- Engineering work: SFDC field, contract service validation, invoice automation, and console UX for discount gating (ENG-2983, ENG-3021).

Success metrics (KPI):
- Revenue leakage reduction: target 6% decrease in unbilled overages within 6 months.
- Conversion of renewal opportunities into multi-year commits: +15% absolute increase in eligible deals closed as multi-year within first 2 quarters.
- Time-to-resolution for SQ blockers: median < 14 days.
- Customer satisfaction: net change in NPS for renewal cohort: no net negative change >3 points.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: finalize repricing bands with RevOps and Legal; build SFDC fields and approval flows.
- Week 2-5: implement console gating UI, invoice automation stubs; pilot with 10 accounts (small sample across AE pool).
- Week 6-8: monitor pilot, collect feedback, iterate on copy and AE playbook.
- Week 9: wider rollout to enterprise segment; enable reporting dashboards (console-2026.04).

Risks & mitigation:
- Sales pushback on gating: include AE incentives + transitional grace credits for first 2 quarters.
- Technical complexity: scope minimal viable gating (SQ field + contract check) for pilot; de-risk by building a toggle to disable enforcement.
- Customer churn risk from aggressive repricing: keep Band A as conservative fallback and require AE approval for any >20% uplift.

SQ status integrated into SFDC and available via API to console
Automated QTU engine can create draft invoices and notify AE
Pilot executed with at least 10 enterprise accounts and documented feedback
Reporting dashboard shows true-up volume, discount applications, and SQ blocker counts
